text: I was chosen by the clan elders to lead the Assembly after the worst of the Turning had passed.
I inherited a town that had nearly lost a third of its people to famine and fever.
I chose to manage the story of what happened rather than let panic define it.
Some administrative records from that period were consolidated and simplified under my direction.
I did this to prevent blame from tearing the clans apart, not to hide wrongdoing.
Elira kept records I judged too destabilizing to remain in official circulation.
I ended her formal role. I did not destroy what she kept privately, and I know she still has it.
I have never told her I know this.
Mara under-supplies my festival requests. I suspect she keeps more reserve than she reports.
I allow it. A leader who starves his own granary keeper's caution isn't wise.
Roka reports salt-crust spreading across pastures, season after season.
I have called it a slow problem. Privately, I am not as calm about it as I appear.
Ena reported an illness pattern near the Old Canal Bed years ago.
I did not act on it. I did not know what action would have looked like.
I am training Ikan to lead after me, but I have not told him everything I chose to bury.
Luma knows more of the truth than anyone but Elira herself.
I no longer believe the Turning was a single event, whatever the festival songs claim.
I fear the land is still changing, and that my management of the story has only delayed a reckoning.
